key_insight: Magnetic Barkhausen Noise and thermoelectric measurements can detect storage-induced changes in flux-cored welding wires, with strong agreement between key signals.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical non-destructive way to screen consumable wire condition before welding, helping avoid use of degraded material in production.
method: Stored rutile flux-cored wires in four environments for 3, 6, and 12 months
Assessed visual condition, Seebeck coefficient, and bulk magnetic properties
Measured Magnetic Barkhausen Noise parameters and compared them statistically with thermoelectric data
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong correlations between magnetic and thermoelectric indicators, including r = 0.99 for the MBN Amplitude-to-Envelope Ratio versus Seebeck Coefficient in two environments.
watch_item: The results are based on a limited set of storage sites and times, so broader validation is needed before routine industrial adoption.
paper_title: Feasibility study of using magnetic and thermoelectric methods for the assessment of storage-induced changes in flux-cored welding wires
